Antiplatelet Agents:

•75 – 150mg from 12 weeks.

High Risk Factors: Moderate risk Factors

- HTN in previous pregnancy. - Age > 40

- Chronic HTN - BMI >35

- DM 1, 2. - Inter pregnancy interval > 10years.

- SLE. - Family history of PTE

- APLS. - Multiple pregnancy

- CKD. - 1st pregnancy.

•Pre – pregnancy counselling – stop ACE, inhibitors, ARB, Thiazides, diuretics.
•Advice: healthy eating, exercise, weight, management and salt reduction.

Timing of Delivery:

⇨CH HTN and Gestational Hypertension, B.P <160/100, Delivery not before 37 weeks

Delivery after 37 weeks according to obstetric review and women choices

⇨Pre – Eclampsia and B.P >160/110: Formulate birth plan

* Decision Making Factors for timing of birth:

•Uncontrolled B.P despite 3 classes of antihypertensive with appropriate doses.
•O2 sat < 90%
•Progressive deterioration in LFT’S, RFT’S, hemolysis, low Plt.
•Ongoing neurological symptoms.
•Abruption.
•REDF in U/A Doppler.

•Non – reassuring CTG/ Still birth.

* Team Involved in Decision Making:

•Senior Obstetrician.
•Anesthetist.
•Neonatologist.

Offer:

-Steroid and mgso4 in pre – Term babies before 37 weeks.

Timing:

-Before 37 weeks if any of above worsening factor.

After 37:

-Initiate within 24 – 48 hours.

Anti – Hypertensives:

* Antenatal Period:

•1st line – labetalol (C/I in Asthma).
•2nd line – nifedipine (C/I with Mgso4).
•3rd line – Methyldopa, (C/I in PP period).

* Postnatal:

•Enalapril – Breast Feeding friendly.
•Nifedipine/amlodipine.
